q: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

items.p: The flowers in the garden behind the old schoolhouse ______ every spring, drawing visitors from across the county who come to see their bright colors.
w: "Blooms" is singular, but the subject "flowers" is plural.
items.e: The plural subject "flowers" takes the plural verb "bloom."

items.p: The ______ new playground opened last weekend, and families from across the city came to try its climbing wall and slides on the first warm day of the year.
w: "Parks'" is plural possessive, but there is one park.
items.e: One park owns the playground, so the singular possessive is "park's."

items.p: Last summer, the research team ______ more than three hundred plant samples from the island's forests, which the scientists are now analyzing in their laboratory.
w: "Last summer" calls for the past tense.
items.e: "Last summer" marks a completed past action, so the verb is "collected."

items.p: The museum invited local artists to submit work for its annual community show, and more than two hundred of ______ responded with paintings, sculptures, and photographs.
items.e: The pronoun refers to the plural "artists," so "them" is correct.

items.p: Each of the volunteers at the animal shelter ______ a short training course before working with the dogs and cats housed there, most of whom are waiting for new homes.
items.e: The subject is "Each," which is singular, not "volunteers."

items.p: All of the ______ uniforms were replaced before the championship game, after the old ones had faded and frayed from many years of washing and wear.
w: "Player's" is singular possessive, but the uniforms belong to many players.
items.e: Many players own the uniforms, so the plural possessive is "players'."

items.p: By the time the rescue boat arrived, the stranded hikers ______ on the small island for nearly two days, surviving on the snacks in their packs.
w: "Wait" is present, but the events are past.
items.e: The waiting happened before the boat arrived (a past event), so the past perfect "had waited" is needed.

items.p: Neither the coach nor the players ______ expecting the storm that suddenly forced the championship game to stop in the third quarter, sending fans running for cover.
w: With "neither… nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the plural "players."
items.e: The verb agrees with "players," the subject closest to it, so it is plural: "were."

items.p: When the company released its annual report in March, ______ showed that sales had risen in every region except the north, where a new competitor had opened several stores.
w: "One" doesn't clearly refer to the report.
items.e: The pronoun refers to the singular "report," so "it" is correct.

items.p: The novelist writes every morning before sunrise, long before the rest of the house is awake; she ______ that the quiet hours before dawn are when her best ideas arrive.
w: The passage is in the present tense.
items.e: The text describes a current habit in the present tense, so "says" keeps the tense consistent.

items.p: The research vessel spent three months at sea last year, and ______ crew collected water samples from more than forty locations across the southern ocean.
items.e: The crew belongs to the singular "vessel," so the possessive is "its."

items.p: The list of ingredients needed for the traditional holiday bread ______ surprisingly short, given how rich the finished loaf tastes: flour, water, salt, yeast, and a spoonful of honey.
items.e: The singular subject "list" takes the singular verb "is."

items.p: The cathedral stands at the center of the old town, surrounded by narrow streets lined with shops and cafés. Built in the twelfth century and restored many times since, ______
c: the cathedral still draws thousands of visitors each year.
thousands of visitors are still drawn to the cathedral each year.
visitors still come by the thousands to see the cathedral.
each year the cathedral is visited by thousands.
w: This says the visitors were built in the twelfth century.
This says the visitors were built and restored.
This places "each year" after the modifier, so it dangles.
items.e: The modifier "Built… since" must be followed directly by what was built: the cathedral.

items.p: Divers exploring the reef last summer made an unexpected discovery. Among the items found in the shipwreck ______ a brass compass, several clay jars, and a small wooden chest still sealed with wax.
w: In this inverted sentence, the subject is the compound list that follows, which is plural.
items.e: The subject (compass, jars, chest) comes after the verb and is plural, so the verb is "were."

items.p: The Kellerman Museum is one of the few museums in the country that ______ their entire collections online, allowing anyone with an internet connection to view the artworks for free.
w: "That" refers to the plural "museums," so the verb must be plural.
items.e: The clause describes the museums (plural) that display their collections, so the verb is "display."

items.p: The city council, after months of debate and several crowded public hearings, finally ______ to approve the plan for a new park on the city's east side.
w: "Voting" can't serve as the main verb.
"Having voted" can't serve as the main verb.
"To vote" can't serve as the main verb.
items.e: The sentence needs a finite main verb for the subject "council," and that is "voted."

items.p: The trail climbed nearly a thousand meters in just four miles, and the afternoon sun was hotter than anyone had expected. Exhausted after the long climb, ______
c: the hikers rested beside the lake before starting down.
the lake was a welcome place for the hikers to rest.
resting beside the lake was what the hikers did.
a rest beside the lake refreshed the hikers.
w: This says the lake was exhausted.
This says the rest was exhausted.
items.e: The modifier "Exhausted after the long climb" must be followed directly by the people who were exhausted: the hikers.
